PostPublish.description:
How a publish was confirmed, and whether the platform API should be called.

`manual_confirmation` is the only honest path for `manual_export` platforms: a human
posts in the official creation console and records the result here. `external_post_id`
records a post id produced outside this workspace (also used for API platforms whose
console was used instead of the API).

`execute_remote` opts into a *real* outbound publish through the platform's official
API: the stored OAuth token is decrypted and used to call the vendor endpoint, and the
returned receipt becomes the post's `external_post_id`. It defaults to `False` so the
historical record-only behaviour is never changed by an older caller.
PostPublish.title: PostPublish

Map/POI jobs stay `pending` until `/run`; a CSV payload or a batch recipe runs now.

The uploaded CSV bytes and the `cities`/`keywords`/`provider_mode` batch recipe are
request-scoped and never persisted, so an import or a multi-city batch has to
execute while the payload is still in memory. A legacy job that pins
`source_provider` + `target_region` keeps the two-step create/run flow.

`source_provider` records the *requested* primary provider; the provider that
actually produced each row is reported per prospect in `raw_metadata.provider`
and aggregated on the job as `sources` (`overpass_osm` / `google_places` /
`fallback_catalog`), so live map data is never confused with the fallback.

options.description:
Answer the preflight without ever granting cookie/credentialed cross-origin access.

Preflight carries no site_key, so the Origin cannot be validated against a channel
account here. The widget authenticates with a Bearer header (never cookies), therefore
the unchecked preflight omits ``Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`` entirely instead of
echoing an unvalidated Origin as credentialed.
